title: Implement an interval merger in Rust that merges overlapping and adjacent intervals
description: Greenfield Rust task: implement merge_intervals(intervals: Vec<[i32; 2]>) -> Vec<[i32; 2]> that sorts intervals by start time then greedily merges overlapping or adjacent ranges.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement merge_intervals in src/lib.rs.

pub fn merge_intervals(mut intervals: Vec<[i32; 2]>) -> Vec<[i32; 2]>

Algorithm:
1. Sort intervals by their start value.
2. Iterate through the sorted list with a result vec.
3. If result is empty or the current interval starts after result.last().end, push it.
4. Otherwise extend result.last().end = max(result.last().end, current.end).

Adjacent intervals (where start == prev.end) should be merged.

All 7 tests in tests/merge_test.rs must pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: Sorts intervals by start value before merging
Merges overlapping intervals by extending the end
Merges adjacent intervals where start == prev.end
Returns empty vec for empty input
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
